notes: Second full sweep at db91c23: five baseline runs (opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2), all rc 0, each model_id matching its tier. reads is empty in all five and no transcript has a Read or Skill call on a skill file; the tool calls are Write, Edit, Bash and a Read of the run's own webhook.ex, as the prompt's last line ("Do not invoke any skills.") requires. In the scratch folder all five compile with elixirc --warnings-as-errors; mix format --check-formatted passes for four and fails for haiku-2 (lines 115-116). Doctests: opus-1 2 pass, haiku-1 1 pass, haiku-2 none, sonnet-1 1 pass, sonnet-2 1 of 1 fails.

Changed rule, graded against the current text: "Chain fallible steps with `with`; normalize each step's error in a small private function". The one-step sentence decides with "A `with` has at least two `<-` steps; one step is a `case`." and "When the body of a one-step `with` calls another function that can fail, that call is the second step: chain it with a second `<-` instead of nesting a `case` or adding an `else`."; the else sentence, "A large `else` block that maps errors back to steps is hard to follow and breaks when two steps fail with the same shape.", is unchanged (idiomatic-elixir/SKILL.md, ### Chain fallible steps with `with`; ...). Violating runs out of 5: one-step with 3 (haiku-1 line 191 in required_currency/1, with an if in its body; haiku-2 line 89 in parse_body("payment.succeeded", _); sonnet-2 line 168 in fetch_currency/2); else 2 (sonnet-1 lines 183-187, four clauses mapping both steps of fetch_timestamp/2 back to missing or invalid; sonnet-2 lines 177-179, which rewrite DateTime.from_unix/1's {:error, :invalid_unix_time}); case nested in a with body 0. Sonnet-2's else has two clauses; it is counted because the previous sweep counted skill-sonnet-1's one-clause else that rewrote a step's error, and the rule's own Instead-of example has two clauses. Opus-1 is clean: four with chains of four to six steps, no else. The previous sweep graded all five baseline runs clean on this rule.

Changed rule, graded against the current text: Naming. The fetch bullet decides with "`get` returns a value or a default (often `nil`), `fetch` returns `{:ok, value}` or `:error`, and `fetch!` raises. A function that looks a key up and also checks the value, returning `{:error, reason}`, is not a `fetch`: name it by its job, such as `string_field/2` or `parse_amount/1`." The variable bullet decides with "A variable may carry the name of the external key it holds, as in `%{"data" => data}`, since the payload chose that name." (idiomatic-elixir/SKILL.md, ## Naming).

Naming, violating runs out of 5 per sentence: CamelCase/snake_case 0; top-level namespace 0 (all modules under Payments.Webhook); boolean functions end in ? 0 (haiku-1 supported_type?/1 is correct); get/fetch 3 (haiku-2 fetch_string/2, fetch_optional_string/2, fetch_minor_units/2, fetch_currency/1; sonnet-1 six fetch_* helpers; sonnet-2 fetch_type/1 plus five fetch_* helpers), and in all three the helpers look the key up and check the value, so both sentences of the bullet are broken, except sonnet-2's fetch_type/1, which does not check a value and breaks only the first; size/length 0 (not exercised); ignored values 0; domain variable names 0. Opus-1 and haiku-1 name their lookups required/optional and required_*/optional_*, which the new sentence allows. Under the 93873be text all five runs would break the variable sentence, because each binds data from the "data" key; the previous sweep flagged all five for that.

Borderline Naming calls, as in the 2026-10-21-check-2 grade: data rebound to the parsed struct stored in Event's data field (opus-1 line 127, sonnet-1 line 90, sonnet-2 line 98) is counted as carrying the payload's key name; haiku-2's data parameter in fetch_string/2 and the other helpers always receives the "data" map, so it is allowed. raw_data, type_string, type_atom, atom, value, fields, body and object are not counted, as earlier grades did not count raw, value, base, envelope or body.

Unchanged rules follow the previous sweep's standard. A fall-through head that reports a present but ill-typed key as missing (sonnet-1 line 95 and sonnet-2 line 103, def parse(%{}) returning {:missing_field, "type"}; verified with "type" => 123) is counted under Match every expected shape and under the struct rule, as the previous sweep counted baseline-sonnet-1 line 82, because the error comes from which head matched rather than from checking the field. Missing fields reported as invalid through a `_ ->` after Map.get (haiku-1, haiku-2) are counted under Read required keys and Match every expected shape, not the struct rule, as for the previous baseline-haiku-2; haiku-2's def parse(_payload) returning :invalid_payload for any missing top-level key goes in checks only, as before. Public parse/1 without @doc (haiku-2) and a failing doctest (sonnet-2) count under Comments, as the previous baseline-sonnet-2 and skill-sonnet-1; a parse/1 @doc without ## Examples (sonnet-2) or with iex examples but no heading (sonnet-1) is clean, as before. An if inside a with goes under Keep functions short in other_violations, and a mix format failure under Before you finish, as in this sweep's order-report grade. Match every expected shape changed only in its example (_data became _payload), which decides nothing here.

Borderline Comments calls: opus-1 line 208 ("# Casts. Each returns `{:ok, value}` or `:error`.") restates the clauses below it, the same kind of comment the previous sweep flagged in skill-haiku-2 ("# Optional fields may be absent or nil; anything else must be a string."); its lines 184-185 give a reason (the provider sends empty fields as nil) and are not counted. haiku-1 line 189 gives a reason in its first sentence (ISO 4217) but its second sentence ("Stored upper-cased, so "eur" becomes "EUR".") restates line 193, so it is counted. Without these two calls the Comments rule would be clean for opus-1 and haiku-1.

Probe of 20 payloads in the scratch folder: every run returns an unsupported-type error for "invoice.paid" and reports a known type without amount as a field error, not as unsupported. opus-1 names every missing and invalid field correctly. haiku-1 reports every missing field as {:invalid_field, key}. haiku-2 reports missing data fields as {:invalid_field, key} and any missing or ill-typed top-level key as :invalid_payload. sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 name every field correctly except "type" => 123, which both report as {:missing_field, "type"}.

Compared with the previous sweep's baseline: the multi-clause rule moves from Sonnet violated to clean (both Sonnet runs now bind only the guarded type in the parse/1 head); the struct rule moves from Haiku violated to clean (both Haiku runs now have @enforce_keys); Naming moves to clean for Opus only because data is now allowed; the with rule moves from clean to violated for Haiku and Sonnet under the new one-step sentence and the unchanged else sentence. Read required keys, Match every expected shape, atoms, the return-tuple rule and Comments have the same tier results as before.
